name: Gibbar
overview: Gibbar is a male figure noted in the biblical record primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. While his tribal affiliation is not explicitly stated, he is associated with the post-exilic community. The mention of Gibeon in Nehemiah 7:25 may relate to the same group or lineage, providing additional context to his historical setting.
namesAndTitles: The name Gibbar means "[young vigorous] man, hero," reflecting strength or valor, though it was not a name given by God. Additionally, the name Gibeon appears in relation to this figure, though without a specific meaning provided in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Gibbar as a descendant of Jacob, indicating his place within the broader covenantal lineage. Beyond this, his family is noted chiefly through his sons, who returned with the exiles to Judah, but no further familial details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Gibbar's significance lies in his role as an ancestor whose descendants participated in the restoration of the Jewish community after captivity. This return marks a critical moment in Israel's history, emphasizing God's faithfulness in preserving His people. The association with Gibeon may also highlight the geographical or communal identity of his lineage during this period.
